messages.author: e1c430550f86b1f6
messages.subject: expose_stan_functions  / user define function variable scope help
parts:
Hi all,

My apology if it's a bit of a newbie question.

Let's say I have a stan model:

Sample Model:

data {
  int N;
  vector[N] y;
  vector[N] x;
}

parameters {
  real beta;
  real<lower=0> sigma;
}

model {
  y ~ normal (beta * x, sigma);
}

For posterior simulation, I have added generated quantities block (and relevant data block):

data {
...
int J;
vector[J] x_tilde

generated quantities {
  vector[J] y_tilde;

  y_tilde <- normal_rng (beta * x_tilde, sigma);
}

So far so good - now I want to explore if it is possible to compute y_tilde with the stanFit obj (i.e. I don't know x_tilde during the fitting process).

From rstan doc - it is mentioned that expose_stan_functions can be use to do posterior simulation outside of generated quantities block.

So, i tried to  move the code in generated quantities block to a separate function:

functions {
  vector stan_gen_rng (vector x_tilde);

  vector stan_gen_rng (vector x_tilde) {
    return (normal_rng(beta * x_tilde, sigma));
  }
}

But, stan_c now complains about variable scope:


rror in stanc(file = file, model_code = model_code, model_name = model_name,  :
  failed to parse Stan model 't50' with error message:
SYNTAX ERROR, MESSAGE(S) FROM PARSER:

variable "beta" does not exist.

ERROR at line 5

  4:      vector stan_gen_rng (vector x_tilde) {
  5:        return (normal_rng(beta * x_tilde, sigma));
                                   ^
  6:      }


Question:
1. is it possible to access variable declared in data & parameters block from user defined functions?
2. If not, what would be the way to do posterior simulation with expose_stan_functions?

Many thanks,

Andy

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: expose_stan_functions  / user define function variable scope help
parts:
On Monday, November 30, 2015 at 4:54:55 AM UTC-5, andy...@cubist-asia.com wrote:
 
Question:
1. is it possible to access variable declared in data & parameters block from user defined functions?
No, unless you pass them as arguments
2. If not, what would be the way to do posterior simulation with expose_stan_functions?

Pass the posterior draws as another argument. Something like

vector stan_gen_rng(matrix beta, vector sigma, vector x_tilde) {
  vector[rows(beta)] y_tilde;
  # beta has sims rows and K columns as in extract(stanfit, "beta")[[1]]
  y_tilde <- beta * x_tilde;
  for (i in 1:rows(beta))
    y_tilde[i] <- y_tilde[i] + normal_rng(0, sigma[i]);
  return y_tilde;
}

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] expose_stan_functions  / user define function variable scope help
parts:
Stan uses C/C++/Java-style scoping, so the only variables
in scope in a function body are the function's arguments and
any locals already defined. It makes functions much more
predictable in terms of their behavior and much easier to
modularize in a standalone way. If they depended on data,
there'd be no way to call them without a data block and
other variables in scope.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: expose_stan_functions / user define function variable scope help
parts:
On Tuesday, December 1, 2015 at 2:05:11 AM UTC-5, Andy Choi wrote:
Thanks for the example. A couple of follow-up questions:

1. If the fitted paremter is a matrix (e.g. chokesly_factor_corr) - how can they be passed into the function?

As a matrix or an array of matrices, in which case the function signature would be a matrix[]. Arguments to user-defined functions are not automatically validated so they cannot be specializations of the basic types.
2. Is there documentation/example I can read somewhere?

All the rules are in the chapter on user-defined functions in the manual, but that doesn't have an example of every single type.

Ben

Ben, many thanks.

Slightly different topic: I'm having some trouble passing arrays from rstan to exposed user defined functions.

Let's say, i have fitted a multivariate normal model via rstan in an object call stanFit with the cholesky_factor_corr called L_Omega_f.

In the user defined function, i have the following signature:

real test1 (matrix[] L_Omega_f);

In R, I would the following:
> stan.LOmega.f <- extract(stanFit, pars="L_Omega_f")[[1]];
> dim(stan.LOmega.f)
[1] 20000     9     9
> test1(stan.LOmega.f)
Error in test1(stan.LOmega.f) :
  VECTOR_ELT() can only be applied to a 'list', not a 'double'

It seems that somehow arrays are not recognized correctly.

In another simple linear regression model, i fitted K beta_c via rstan and try to pass the values back to 2 different user defined functions:

real test1 (matrix foo);
real test2 (real[,] foo);

in R:
> stan.beta.c   <- extract(stanFit, pars="beta_c")[[1]];
> dim(stan.beta.c)
[1] 20000     9
> test1(stan.beta.c)
....OK....
> test2(stan.beta.c)
Error in test2(stan.beta.c) :
  VECTOR_ELT() can only be applied to a 'list', not a 'double'

I'm still on stan/rstan 2.7.

Many thanks,

Andy
